title: STM32: SPI.read(n) fails if n > 1 (regression)
body: I am driving an EEPROM over hardware SPI on a Pyboard D SF6W using SPI(2) at 5 MHz. The same board and EEPROM setup worked in the past, and it still works on a Pyboard D SF2W running MicroPython v1.18-355-g9ab66b50c-dirty. On the SF6W with MicroPython v1.22.1, a one-byte read returns the correct value, but a multi-byte read returns a bytes object of the correct length containing zeros. SoftSPI works with reads of any length. A logic-analyzer trace shows the EEPROM transmitting the correct bytes and otherwise identical CS, clock, and data signals for single- and multi-byte reads. Looking at the STM32 SPI code, multi-byte transfers appear to use DMA while single-byte transfers do not.

symptoms_visible: On my Pyboard D SF6W with MicroPython v1.22.1, SPI(2).read(n) returns zero bytes when n is greater than one, although a one-byte read is correct.
The EEPROM sends the expected data on MISO according to the logic analyzer, and the same setup works with SoftSPI and older firmware.
N0.label: N0 multi-byte hardware SPI reads reported

symptoms_visible: The EEPROM still returns zeros for multi-byte hardware-SPI reads on firmware from v1.19.1 onward, while v1.18 passes.
The SPI pin configuration is the same on the working and failing firmware.
Simple tied-level, loopback, and toggled-MISO tests do not consistently reproduce what I see with the EEPROM.
N1.label: N1 regression range and reproduction limits established

symptoms_visible: My EEPROM driver works with hardware SPI when I replace its multi-byte spi.read() calls with write_readinto() calls that use different write and read buffers.
The normal spi.read() path can return its transmitted fill value rather than the value present on MISO.
N2.label: N2 in-place transfer condition isolated

symptoms_visible: The normal optimized build still gives incorrect multi-byte hardware-SPI reads.
A build that compiles the STM32F7 DMA HAL code with -O2 passes my full EEPROM test.
Changing optimization or adding a very small call delay can change whether the read fails.
N3.label: N3 optimization-sensitive DMA behavior confirmed

symptoms_visible: The EEPROM multi-byte reads work correctly for me on the branch containing the root-cause patch.
A second affected setup also reads correctly with that branch.
N4.label: N4 root-cause patch verified

symptoms_visible: Multi-byte spi.read() calls now return the bytes present on MISO, and the EEPROM passes its full test using hardware SPI.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you test additional firmware versions and narrow down when the regression appeared?
What is the newest working release and the oldest failing release?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the pre-built firmware from the website. v1.18 is the most recent version that passes; v1.19.1 and later fail, so it appeared between January and June 2022.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same EEPROM test also fails on v1.18, so I cannot identify a firmware regression boundary.
v1.18 passes and the first failing build is another build from the same early-2022 development interval.

question_patterns: Which SPI peripheral is affected, and can you print the SPI pins after reproducing the problem?
Are Y6, Y7, and Y8 still configured for SPI2 in both the working and failing firmware?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am using SPI(2). On both v1.18 and v1.22.1, Y6 is B13 AF5_SPI2, Y7 is C2 AF5_SPI2, and Y8 is C3 AF5_SPI2. The pin modes and pull-down settings are the same.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After the failed read, Y7 is no longer in AF5_SPI2 mode and has been changed to a GPIO output.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce it with MISO tied high or low, with MOSI linked to MISO, or with a simple toggling source?
What happens with a standalone electrical reproduction instead of the EEPROM?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Tying MISO to a level does not demonstrate the EEPROM failure here. Linking MOSI and MISO also passes, and a JK flip-flop toggling MISO returns the expected 0x55 bytes. With the EEPROM, however, multi-byte reads consistently fail even though its MISO trace is correct.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The loopback test uses a different wire colour, but its returned bytes are unchanged.

edges.comment: Thread c1-c11: the reporter narrowed the release range, confirmed SPI(2) and unchanged alternate-function pin configuration, and documented false-negative standalone probes. A second affected user reproduced unreliable hardware-SPI reads from an SPI2 flash device while SoftSPI and loopback worked; that corroboration is folded into the simulated user side as volunteered information.

question_patterns: Does write_readinto() work if the transmit and receive buffers are different objects?
Can you replace the multi-byte read with a full-duplex transfer using separate buffers and rerun the EEPROM test?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I replaced the multi-byte reads with spi.write_readinto() using different buffers, and the driver now works with hardware SPI on STM32 running the latest firmware.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The EEPROM still returns zeros when write_readinto() uses two different buffers.
Separate buffers work with a bytearray receive buffer but not with an immutable receive object.

question_patterns: When spi.read() is given a nonzero write value, does it return that fill value instead of the MISO data?
Can you test an inverted MOSI-to-MISO signal with spi.read(n, 0x55) and report the raw bytes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With an inverter between MOSI and MISO, spi.read(5, 0x55) returned b'UUUUU' instead of the inverted b'\xaa\xaa\xaa\xaa\xaa'. A single-byte read still returned the input correctly.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The multi-byte call returns the inverted MISO value b'\xaa\xaa\xaa\xaa\xaa', so it is not returning the transmitted fill bytes.

edges.comment: Thread c12-c18: one affected user inspected extmod/machine_spi.c and volunteered that machine_spi.read() passes the same allocated buffer as both transmit and receive; the destination node records this volunteered fact. Both affected users then tested separate-buffer and fill-byte behavior. The answers preserve only the observed API results; the DMA/cache mechanism is engineer-side inference.

question_patterns: Can you rebuild with DEBUG or different optimization levels and report which builds reproduce the failure?
Does recompiling the STM32F7 DMA HAL source with -O2 instead of -Os change the result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A DEBUG build works. Builds using -O1 or -O2 work here, while the normal -Os build fails. Recompiling stm32f7xx_hal_dma.c with -O2 also makes SPI work.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failure is identical with DEBUG, -O1, -O2, and -Os, including when the DMA HAL file is rebuilt separately.
Rebuilding the related SPI HAL file with -O2 works as well as rebuilding the DMA HAL file.

question_patterns: Do delays around HAL_DMA_Start_IT() prevent the failure?
Can you vary the timing around the DMA-start calls and report the observed result?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Adding delays before and after both DMA-start calls initially did not help. On a later test, a short delay before the first HAL_DMA_Start_IT(), even HAL_Delay(0), was enough to make it work.

question_patterns: Can you build and test PR #13549 on the EEPROM board?
Please run the full EEPROM test with the build that compiles the F7 DMA HAL using -O2.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built #13549, and the EEPROM board now passes the full test, which is quite rigorous.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The #13549 build still returns zeros in the full EEPROM test.

edges.comment: Thread c19-c38: commit-level bisection was inconsistent between machines, but optimization-sensitive behavior was repeatable. PR #13549 was an optimization-based workaround and its build was tested successfully; it is evidence about timing/cache sensitivity, not the final root-cause fix.

question_patterns: Please test the linked branch on the board that reproduces the problem and tell me what you see.
Can you rerun the same SPI and EEPROM tests with this candidate branch?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Done. The fix works in the standalone test, and it works for me on the EEPROM setup too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate branch still returns transmitted fill bytes or zeros instead of the MISO data.
The candidate branch passes the EEPROM test on one affected Pyboard D, but the second board has not been retested yet.

edges.comment: Thread c39-c42: this is pre-landing verification of the root-cause branch. Both affected users are folded into one simulated user side, and the answer contains only their observed test outcomes.

solution.intent: Fix STM32F7 DMA cache coherency for the in-place full-duplex transfer used by spi.read(), so speculative Cortex-M7 cache activity cannot substitute stale transmit/fill data for bytes received by DMA.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the STM32 DMA cache-maintenance fix from the linked root-cause patch so spi.read(), which uses one buffer for transmit and receive, safely receives DMA data on Cortex-M7. Separate write/read buffers and compiling HAL_DMA_Start_IT() with -O2 may avoid the symptom, but they are workarounds rather than the final correction.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter and second tester supplied raw transfer results, optimization-dependent build results, and candidate-branch verification. Engineers connected these observations to Cortex-M7 speculative cache line fills and a DMA cache-coherency failure when spi.read() reuses one memory region for both transmit and receive. That mechanism is an engineer inference, not something the reporter independently diagnosed.

edges.comment: Final resolution from c39-c42: the root-cause patch supersedes the separate-buffer, delay, DEBUG, and -O2 workarounds. The candidate branch was verified by both affected setups before the issue was considered fixed.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as a Cortex-M7/STM32F7 DMA cache-coherency problem affecting the in-place transmit/receive buffer used by spi.read(), with speculative cache activity explaining the optimization- and timing-sensitive behavior.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: single-byte non-DMA reads work, the logic analyzer shows correct MISO data, separate write/read buffers work, same-buffer reads can return transmitted fill bytes, and changing optimization around the DMA HAL changes the result.

Must not treat wiring, SPI pin configuration, baud rate, or the successful loopback/tied-level probes as disproving the firmware bug; the EEPROM and flash-device traces show correct external bus data.

Must not present separate buffers, DEBUG builds, added delays, or compiling the DMA HAL with -O2 as the permanent root fix; these are diagnostic workarounds that alter whether the cache-sensitive failure appears.
Must have the affected user verify a build containing the root-cause fix on the reproducing hardware before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly experienced MicroPython hardware and driver developer; comfortable building firmware, reading C source, using logic analyzers and oscilloscopes, constructing digital test circuits, and designing controlled SPI experiments.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, methodical, and candid about uncertainty; reports exact firmware versions, code, electrical setup, and raw outputs; challenges hypotheses politely when experiments disagree.
